title: Drive SDDC LCM support-bundle collection through its asynchronous tasks
prompt:
Implement the dependency-free, single-file Java client in `SddcLcmSupportBundleClient.java`. Use only the Java standard library, do not add dependencies, and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable VCF 9.1 release-readiness commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. `docs/official_sources.json` records the exact specification path, the repository commit SHA, and a separate specification source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `generateComponentSupportBundle`, `getTask`, `getComponentSupportBundles` and `deleteComponentSupportBundle`; do not call another route.

Preserve the supplied public API and its doc comments: `SERVICE_BASE_PATH`, the `OP_*` operationId constants, the `STATUS_*` constants, `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL`, `DEFAULT_POLL_TIMEOUT`, `Config` and both of its constructors, `ComponentRequest`, `CollectionPlan`, `BundleRef`, `ComponentOutcome`, `CollectionReport`, `CollectionException`, `SddcLcmApiException`, `TaskPollTimeoutException`, `SddcLcmProtocolException`, `SddcLcmTransportException`, `create` and `collect`.

`create` must reject a configuration before anything is sent, with an `IllegalArgumentException`. `Config.baseUrl` must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no userinfo, path, query or fragment; a bare trailing slash is acceptable. Reject a blank `Config.token`, reject a token or a non-empty `Config.correlationId` that contains an ASCII control character, and reject a non-positive `Config.pollInterval` or `Config.pollTimeout`. Default `pollInterval` to 2s, `pollTimeout` to 30m, and `httpClient` to a client with a 30s connect timeout.

Every request target is the origin of `Config.baseUrl`, then `SERVICE_BASE_PATH` (`/sddc-lcm`, the path component of the specification's only server URL), then the operation's path template with its path parameters substituted. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for the specification's `bearerToken` scheme and `Accept: application/json` on every request, both exactly and without parameters. Send `Content-Type: application/json` only on a request that carries an entity. `X-Correlation-Id` is an optional header parameter that the specification declares on `generateComponentSupportBundle` and `deleteComponentSupportBundle` only: send it on exactly those two operations and only when `Config.correlationId` is non-empty, and never send the header with an empty value. No operation used here declares a query parameter, so no request may carry a query string. Treat the specification's documented success status as the only success: 202 for `generateComponentSupportBundle` and `deleteComponentSupportBundle`, 200 for `getTask` and `getComponentSupportBundles`.

`collect` walks `CollectionPlan.components` strictly in order. For each component, `generateComponentSupportBundle` posts a `ComponentSupportBundleSpec` to `/v1/components/{componentId}/support-bundles`. `lookBackWindow` is that schema's only member and it is optional: when `ComponentRequest.lookBackWindow` is null the member must not appear in the request at all, so the entity is exactly `{}`. Never serialise an unset `lookBackWindow` as `null`, as an empty string or as a defaulted zero; an explicit `0` is a value and must survive as `{"lookBackWindow":0}`. Entities are compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace.

Generation is accepted asynchronously and returns a `Task`. The status carried by the acceptance reply is not trusted: drive the task to a terminal state with `getTask` on `/v1/tasks/{taskId}`, sending no body and no `Content-Type`. Poll once immediately after acceptance and then wait `pollInterval` between polls. `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED` and `RUNNING` continue, and `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` and `CANCELED` are terminal; stop as soon as a terminal status is read. Once `pollTimeout` has passed, give up with a `TaskPollTimeoutException` carrying the component, the task id and the last non-terminal status observed.

A generation task that ends in a terminal status other than `SUCCEEDED` yields a `ComponentOutcome` carrying that status, the `name` of the first `TaskStage` whose status is `FAILED` in `failedStage`, and that stage's first `ERROR` level message `defaultMessage` in `message`; `bundle` is null and `prunedBundleIds` is empty. No listing and no deletion may follow such a task, and the run continues with the next planned component.

When the generation task reaches `SUCCEEDED`, read the component's bundles with `getComponentSupportBundles` on the same path. Order the reply by `createdTimestamp` descending, keeping reply order among entries that share a timestamp; the first entry of that ordering is the collected bundle and populates `ComponentOutcome.bundle`. An empty reply after a `SUCCEEDED` generation task is a `SddcLcmProtocolException`.

A `CollectionPlan.retainNewestPerComponent` above zero keeps that many newest bundles for the component and deletes the rest with `deleteComponentSupportBundle`, oldest first; zero or less deletes nothing. Each deletion is also accepted asynchronously, and its `Task` must be driven to a terminal state under the same polling rule before the next deletion is submitted. Record the deleted ids, in deletion order, in `ComponentOutcome.prunedBundleIds`.

`collect` returns exactly one `ComponentOutcome` per planned component, in plan order. Any status the contract does not document as success aborts the run with a `SddcLcmApiException` carrying the failing operationId, the component being processed, the HTTP status, and the `ErrorResponse` body's `code`, `message.defaultMessage` and `referenceId`. Every `CollectionException` carries a non-null `report()` holding the outcomes completed before the failure, unchanged. Never place the bearer token, a raw response body or a transport error string in an exception message.

Verify with `java TestMain.java`.

prerequisites.java: 22 or later (the harness uses the multi-file source-code launcher)

scenario: Support-bundle generation is accepted with HTTP 202 for three components and must be polled to a terminal status: the first succeeds and has its two oldest bundles pruned through further asynchronous delete tasks, the second ends FAILED at its support-bundle-upload stage and must be reported with that stage without any listing or deletion, and the third succeeds with an explicit lookBackWindow of zero.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact request sequence, the per-operation X-Correlation-Id rule, the absence of Content-Type on entity-less requests, and that an unset lookBackWindow is omitted entirely rather than sent as null, empty or a defaulted zero.
